title: Why a thermostat lets the temperature swing a little
examples: Why doesn't my room stay at exactly the set temperature?
What is hysteresis in a thermostat?
Why does the heating switch on and off?

explain.say: Set a thermostat to 20 degrees and the room does not stay at exactly 20. It wobbles gently up and down around it, and that is on purpose.

draw.text: Why a thermostat lets the temperature swing a little

explain.say: The heater switches on when the room cools to a little below the target, say 19.5 degrees. It stays on while the room warms up.
It switches off only when the room is a little above the target, say 20.5 degrees, and then the room slowly cools again. This gap between the on and off points is called hysteresis, or the dead band.

Without the gap, the heater would click on and off every few seconds whenever the room hovered right at 20, wearing out the switch and the boiler. A small swing keeps things comfortable and the machine lasting.

faq.q: What is hysteresis in a thermostat?
faq.a: It is the deliberate gap between the temperature that turns the heater on and the one that turns it off. The room swings gently between the two instead of the heater flicking on and off constantly.

faq.q: Why doesn't the thermostat keep the room at exactly the set temperature?
faq.a: A simple heater is either fully on or fully off, so the temperature always overshoots a little each way. The thermostat lets it swing within a small range to avoid rapid switching.
asks: Why does my room temperature go up and down?

faq.a: Short cycling is when a heater or air conditioner switches on and off too often. It wastes energy and wears out parts, which the hysteresis gap helps prevent.
asks: Why does my boiler keep turning on and off?

faq.a: Many learn how quickly your home heats and cools, and switch on early or ease off before reaching the target. Some boilers can also run at part power, which keeps the temperature steadier.
asks: How do smart thermostats keep the temperature steady?

faq.a: In air conditioners, pumps that fill a water tank between a low and a high level, and electronic circuits that must ignore small jitters in a signal.

facts: Many home thermostats use a swing of around half a degree to a degree around the set point.
Hysteresis is also used in electronic circuits called Schmitt triggers to ignore small signal jitter.

quiz.say: Why does a thermostat set to 20 degrees turn the heater off at 20.5 instead of exactly 20?

options.show: To stop the heater switching on and off too often
options.say: To stop the heater switching on and off too often

quiz.why: The gap stops rapid on-off switching while keeping the average temperature near 20.

wrong.1: Sensors read 20 degrees fine; the gap is deliberate.
wrong.2: The gap keeps the average near 20, not colder.
